text: In October, a farmer in Punjab harvests his rice.
The field is left covered in straw.
He has about three weeks to sow wheat, and the straw is in the way.
Machines can pick it up. But they are few, and no one can tell him when one will come.
Straw that is not picked up in time gets burned.
That is the main reason for the fires, and the smoke becomes the air of every village and city downwind.
So we built StrawLink: an app that anticipates the need, before it becomes a fire.
say: So we built Straw Link: an app that anticipates the need, before it becomes a fire.

text: It knows which fields will be ready, plans a machine for each one, and tells the farmer exactly when, so he does not have to burn.
It starts weeks before the harvest.
From satellite images, StrawLink watches two hundred fields near Sangrur turn from green to gold, and works out when each will be cut.
say: From satellite images, Straw Link watches two hundred fields near Sangrur turn from green to gold, and works out when each will be cut.

text: Then, every morning, it plans the day, and by half past seven the machines are on the road.
A baler packs the straw into bales,
and a truck carries them to a plant, where straw is fuel instead of smoke.
When the plants are full, a Super Seeder takes over and sows the wheat straight through the straw.
Either way, nothing is burned.
And the officer in charge can finally answer the hardest question: are there enough machines?
At this pace, everything harvested so far is cleared in ten days, with twenty-two left before sowing.
Double the balers and nothing improves, because trucks are the limit.
Add trucks, and the day clears twice as much.
